stimulus.source_note: Engraving after Johannes Stradanus, Nova Reperta series, about 1600, public domain (Metropolitan Museum of Art, CC0); Waldseemuller map, 1507, public domain (Library of Congress).
stimulus.text: Engraving from the Nova Reperta series, after Johannes Stradanus, about 1600. It shows the Italian explorer Amerigo Vespucci landing in the Americas, holding a navigational instrument, with his ships at anchor behind him and a Native woman in a hammock before him. The engraving is titled 'America.' The set also includes Martin Waldseemuller's world map of 1507, the first map to use the name America for the western continents.

stem: In the engraving, Vespucci stands holding a navigational instrument while a Native woman reclines in a hammock, and European ships anchor behind him. Which claim about European views of the Americas is best supported by this image?

options.text: Europeans saw the Americas as a new world to be measured, named, and claimed
Europeans believed the Americas were empty of people before they arrived
Europeans believed the Americas were part of Asia and sailed there only to trade
Europeans saw Native peoples as equal partners in exploring the Americas

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
